title: Telemetry sieve and latency heatmap pipeline for per-request inference KPIs
creator: Sana Kapoor
description:
Problem: Latency and error signals for per-request LLM inference are scattered across multiple telemetry streams (runtime spans, Prometheus metrics, and logs). Teams building SLAs and automated rollouts need a single, low-noise per-request KPI stream to power heatmaps and root-cause flows in the Console. Current ingestion duplicates labels, has high cardinality spikes, and lacks stable request IDs for cross-signal joins.

Goal: Build a telemetry "sieve" service that sits between the runtime sidecars and our backend collectors to: 1) canonicalize and enrich per-request attributes, 2) deduplicate/merge concurrently emitted metrics and spans, 3) apply tenant-aware sampling and cardinality controls, and 4) emit two harmonized outputs: compact Prometheus-remote_write-friendly series for SLO dashboards and full OTLP traces/metrics for detailed debugging. The pipeline will also precompute a latency heatmap histogram and percentiles per model/route to drive the new Console heatmap panel.

Scope:
- Lightweight sieve sidecar/agent for Dedicated/Private nodes and a gateway for Hosted nodes.
- Label canonicalizer (model, route, region, tier, rollout_id) and stable request_id propagation across traces/logs/metrics.
- Deduplication rules and a merge policy for near-duplicate spans/metrics emitted by SDKs and runtime.
- Adaptive sampling: preserve high-res traces for anomalies and SLOs; aggressive roll-up for high-cardinality noisy labels.
- Heatmap pre-aggregation: streaming histogram buckets, rollup TTL, per-route retention window.
- Dual output: compressed Prometheus-compatible timeseries + enriched OTLP envelopes to long-term storage.

Approach:
1) Prototype sieve as a stateless streaming filter (Rust) with small in-memory LRU for recent request fingerprints.
2) Define a canonical label set and a compact encoding for Prometheus remote_write (histogram + summary buckets).
3) Add a signal to the runtime SDK to attach a stable request_id and route metadata.
4) Build a rollout plan: deploy sieve as a canary in one region/model pair, compare telemetry volumes and latency deltas, and validate Console heatmap correctness.

Constraints & Risks:
- Added hop could increase telemetry tail-latency; require <25ms p95 added latency in canary.
- Misconfigured sampling risks losing debug signals; preserve raw OTLP for 1% of traffic as safety net.
- Cardinality control needs tenant-specific overrides to avoid breaking large customers.

Why this is different from previous work: instead of broad ingestion refactors, this ticket focuses on an inline filter that actively merges and reduces noisy per-request signals and emits pre-aggregated heatmaps specifically tuned for inference workloads (short bursts, KV cache hits/misses, variable seq-lens).
acceptance_criteria: Sieve component deployed in canary region and processing telemetry for at least one active model route
Stable request_id is present on >=99.5% of traces/metrics for the canary traffic
Prometheus output volume reduced by >=35% for canary without degrading observed application traces
Console latency heatmap renders matching percentiles to within 2% of raw OTLP-derived computation for test prompts
End-to-end added telemetry latency from runtime SDK -> backend collectors is <25ms p95 in canary
Integration tests for deduplication rules and adaptive sampling with synthetic spike scenarios
Runbook updated with troubleshooting steps and tenant override controls
comments: 2025-02-14 - Sana Kapoor: Scoped initial prototype, pairing Miguel with runtime SDK team. Confluence spec linked.
2025-02-20 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented request fingerprinting and local LRU. Early benchmark: memory 8MB per 100k active fingerprints.
2025-02-27 - Design review (Jordan Li): Suggested adding explicit 'rollout_id' label to correlate canary traffic with model deploys.
2025-03-01 - QA (Priya Nair): Synthetic spike test shows heatmap matches raw computation within 1.8% for 95th percentile.
2025-03-03 - Security (TBD): Confirmed no PII transformations required, flagged tenant override ACL for Private installs.
notes: Trade-off: Choosing a small LRU cache to keep component stateless under autoscaling; accepts occasional missed dedups in exchange for predictable memory footprint.
Decision: Use Prometheus remote_write histogram best-practices and encode pre-bucketed histograms to avoid high-series cardinality.
Follow-up: If canary meets success criteria, schedule Dedicated-sidecar packaging and operator helm chart work in next cycle.
Performance observation: Rust prototype 3.4x faster than initial Go PoC on synthetic encoding benchmark.
